The scaling cliff

Greenfield demos hit a cliff

Greenfield demo

No legacy to respect, so the task fits in context.

10M-line brownfield

Unwritten conventions overflow any 200K–2M token window; rework estimated at ~30–60%†

Three structural properties

Context is finite and fragile; context must be explicit; output is probabilistic.

† Handbook author estimate; no controlled study

The scaling cliff

Window size is not focus

Liu et al., TACL 2024

Accuracy is highest at the start and end of context, lowest in the middle.

Five PROSE constraints

Direct levers: Progressive Disclosure, Reduced Scope, Orchestrated Composition. Also: Safety Boundaries, Explicit Hierarchy.

Operating model

From hero builders to an enabling CoE

1 · Hero pilot

Top builders prove it works; what they learn stays with them.

2 · Enabling CoE

A small, time-boxed team encodes reusable workflows and coaches other teams.

3 · Advisory guardrails

Guidance replaces gatekeeping so the CoE never becomes an approval bottleneck.

Operating model

Five layers, five owners

Primitives as code

Seven versioned primitives (instructions, agents, skills, prompts, memory, specs, hooks) ship like internal packages.

Operating model

A new function: three concerns

Domain Specialist · WHAT

Owns the procedure, rules, success criteria, and eval.

Agentic Workflow Engineer · HOW

Owns how skills compose, including PROSE-level composition and evals.

Agent Operations Specialist · OPERATIONS

Owns cost, traces, eval drift, and rate limits at scale.

Operations emerges only at scale, not on day one.

Metrics & evals

Faster coding is not faster delivery

Denominator problem

At a 30% coding share, a 50% reduction in coding time saves 15%.

Quality discount

Rework and downstream debugging erase part of the speed gain.

Attribution problem

Crediting results to AI or developer alone misleads.

Lab finding: 55.8% less time on one JavaScript task

Metrics & evals

Metrics grow up in three stages

1 · Activity

Lines of code, PR volume, raw acceptance rate: more code, not better software.

2 · Flow and quality

Time-to-confident-merge, review rejection rate, and 30-day rework rate.

3 · Outcomes and evals

Cost per outcome, defect escape rate, human intervention, golden dataset evaluations.

Usage metrics show association, not causation.

Metrics & evals

Which gate catches it?

Programmatic-internal

Schema, lint, type check, unit tests, grounded lookups.

Judgement-internal

A goal-steward re-reads the spec: still on goal?

Programmatic-external

Independent CI test runner or cold-reader rubric outside the agent.

Judgement-external

A human checkpoint: review, approval, or sign-off.

Process economics

The honest Year-1 bill

Hold through the valley

Expect 60–90 days of slower delivery; context debt, not tool failure, drives it.

† Handbook author estimates for a ten-person team

Process economics

The same task, an 8.5× bill

Undesigned loop $41.01

File by file on a frontier model; re-read, re-plan, retry.

Designed loop $4.81

Plan once, batch edits, route to a cheaper model, verify.

Identical output

Same nineteen files, same passing tests; only the workflow design differs.

Illustrative single run, not a benchmark

Live exercise

Debug one prompt

Scope context

3,800 flat lines become 450 scoped lines.

Stable prefix

Cache hits rise from 0% to 80%+.

Tool subset

65 tools every turn become six scoped tools.

Routed models

Fifteen frontier retries become plan, execute, and a two-round cap.

$41.01 → $4.81 per run

Illustrative model, not vendor pricing

Bottlenecks

Where engineer time goes next

Review gets harder

Agent output looks plausible and passes tests, yet may hide subtle misunderstandings.

† Handbook author projection, not survey data

Bottlenecks

Whack-a-mole in the pipeline

Intake starves

Product cannot supply dev-ready specs fast enough; size and ground specs first.

Review drowns

Plausible diffs flood reviewers; use one file per agent and a two-round cap.

QA lags

Features outrun manual cycles; run deterministic tests outside the agent.

Bottlenecks

Roles evolve, judgment stays

Senior engineers

Implementers become context architects: architecture, context engineering, escalated reviews, mentoring.

Tech leads

Task assigners become orchestrators across humans and agents, owning the feedback loop.

Junior engineers

Code writers become AI-augmented contributors who review output, write specs, diagnose failures.

Guardrails

Layered security, budgeted AI

CodeQL

Deterministic analysis: identical results until query pack or CLI version changes.

AI Scan

Repositories: Public preview. Pull requests: GA; advisory, no merge blocks.

Copilot Autofix

Suggests fixes for CodeQL alerts; humans review and test before merging.

Cost rule

Start small, measure cost against coverage, then expand scope.

Guardrails

Two computers, one program

Strong-form supervision

The agent never holds merge or deploy credentials; gates run after its turn.

Where it exists today

Copilot cloud agent: one permitted branch. gh-aw safe-outputs: separate permissioned jobs apply requests.

Field gotchas

Six anti-patterns, six recoveries

GotchaRecovery
Monolithic promptSplit into scoped instructions and skills
Trust fallRun tests, check git diff
Same-file collisionsOne file, one agent
Unfixed primitivesPatch the instruction or skill
Almost-done trapCommit the 90%, finish fresh
Cost runawayTwo retries, then decompose or escalate

Next 90 days

A 30-60-90 plan

Days 1–30 · Charter

Charter a time-boxed enabling CoE, baseline three process costs, lock strong-form PR security gates.

Days 31–60 · Metrics

Shift the dashboard to time-to-confident-merge and rework; ship three cost-engineered loops.

Days 61–90 · Scale

Pilot targeted AI scanning beside CodeQL; automate golden-dataset evals per product.

Responsible AIWhich non-negotiables protect trust?

Room check

Three scenarios, three decisions

1 · Board metric

AI-generated lines are up. Pick: acceptance rate, time-to-confident-merge, or seat count?

2 · Cost lever

Sixty-five tools load every turn. Pick: tool subset, model router, or bigger window?

3 · Gate choice

Tests pass, wrong feature built. Pick: more tests, design checkpoint, or lint?
